regions.name: The Western Teeth
regions.terrain: mountain, the western third of the great range, breaking down into wooded hills
regions.water: snowmelt streams running south into the forest
regions.climate: cold; long hard winter, short summer
regions.notes: Empty high country. No people holds it.

regions.name: The Snowhead
regions.terrain: mountain, the middle and highest part of the great range
regions.water: snowfields and ice; meltwater south into the basin
regions.climate: very cold; snow most of the year on the heights
regions.notes: The highest ground on the sheet. Few ways through.

regions.name: The Scree Marches
regions.terrain: mountain, high broken mountains of scree and cliff with many passes
regions.water: meltwater in every gully; tarns; streams south to the steppe
regions.climate: cold; long hard winter, loud thaw
regions.notes: Held in passing by the Column (god-stone). The Graith, the slow people of the rock, in its eastern heights.

regions.name: The High Table
regions.terrain: valley, a wide flat high basin ringed by mountains, meadow and worked land
regions.water: the Brenn through the floor, streams from every side
regions.climate: cool; hard winter, early snow on the rim
regions.notes: Held by the Arroway (god-war).

regions.name: The Folds
regions.terrain: forest, deep dark forest over broken folded hills, valleys hidden one from the next
regions.water: a stream at the bottom of every fold
regions.climate: cool and wet; long snowy winter
regions.notes: Held by the Ussel (god-secrets).

regions.name: The Deepwood
regions.terrain: forest, a great old lowland forest of oak and beech
regions.water: many small streams west to the sea; standing pools
regions.climate: temperate and wet; hard winter
regions.notes: The Thessen (god-beasts) hold its north-eastern edge only. The rest is wild.

regions.name: The Mast Vale
regions.terrain: valley, river country between the forest edge and the high rim, wet ground along the river
regions.water: the Mastwater; fen along it
regions.climate: temperate; hard winter, wet autumn
regions.notes: Held by the Thessen (god-beasts) at its western edge.

regions.name: The North Heath
regions.terrain: highland, open brown upland heath and worn low hills, the northern half of a wide shallow bowl
regions.water: few streams; peat pools
regions.climate: windy and cool; hard winter
regions.notes: Grazed by the Hethren.

regions.name: The South Heath
regions.terrain: highland, open brown upland heath and worn low hills, the southern half of a wide shallow bowl
regions.water: few streams; springs on its southern edge
regions.climate: windy and cool; hard winter
regions.notes: Grazed by the Hethren.

regions.name: The Dun Back
regions.terrain: hill, one long dark bare hill mass in the middle of the bowl, with the outline of a great animal lying asleep
regions.water: none on the surface
regions.climate: windy and cool; the ground a little warm
regions.notes: Under the star's center. The Hethren do not graze it.

regions.name: The Gap Vale
regions.terrain: valley, a long vale under the basin rim where the rivers meet and run east
regions.water: the Brenn and the Mastwater join here as the Sarn
regions.climate: temperate, dry to the east
regions.notes: Open country. The Hethren come down to it in winter.

regions.name: The Pale Steppe
regions.terrain: steppe, wide pale grass to the edge of sight
regions.water: the Pallow; little else
regions.climate: dry; bitter winter wind, hot summer
regions.notes: The Lowlamp (god-dreams) winter at its southern edge and travel its road.

regions.name: The Rattlereed
regions.terrain: marsh, a long reed marsh and wet wood where the river divides and joins
regions.water: the Sarn in many threads
regions.climate: dry air, wet ground; hard freeze in winter
regions.notes: Held by the Sallow, the reed folk.

regions.name: The Far Grass
regions.terrain: steppe, open grass running south and east to low coast hills
regions.water: the Pallow
regions.climate: dry; hot summer
regions.notes: Open. The Lowlamp trains cross it.

regions.name: The Flood Meadows
regions.terrain: valley, river country of flood meadow, willow and poplar
regions.water: the Sarn, broad and brown; the Aver leaving it
regions.climate: temperate; spring floods
regions.notes: Held by the Weirfolk (god-rivers).

regions.name: The Old Low Country
regions.terrain: plain, old farmed low country between two rivers, with a rocky headland on the coast
regions.water: the Sarn to the north and west, the Aver to the east
regions.climate: mild for this land; wet autumn
regions.notes: The kingdom of Averley, godless, old and rooted.

regions.name: The Tally Meadows
regions.terrain: plain, low open river country, water meadow and worked land down to a bay
regions.water: the lower Sarn, the Chalkwater, the bay
regions.climate: mild; wet autumn, river low in late summer
regions.notes: Held by the Marrans (god-trade).

regions.name: The Sump
regions.terrain: marsh, wet ground and marsh where the limestone forest drops to the low country
regions.water: standing water; streams that come out of the rock
regions.climate: mild and wet
regions.notes: No one holds it.

regions.name: The Holed Wood
regions.terrain: forest, old forest on broken pale limestone, sinkholes, streams that go into the ground
regions.water: streams that run a while and vanish; water at the bottom of sinkholes
regions.climate: temperate and wet; hard winter, late spring
regions.notes: Held by the player's people, unnamed.

regions.name: The White Ribs
regions.terrain: coast, bare pale limestone ribs and thin wood above a cliffed shore
regions.water: almost none on the surface
regions.climate: wet and windy
regions.notes: Empty but for fowlers and a few fishers.

regions.name: The Shore Hills
regions.terrain: hill, dry rocky hills above the south-east shore
regions.water: the Pallow's mouth
regions.climate: dry and warm
regions.notes: Thinly peopled.

regions.name: The Green Sea
regions.terrain: sea, the western and southern sea
regions.water: salt
regions.climate: open water; winter storms
regions.notes: No one sails out of sight of land.

features.name: The Mastwater
features.notes: Rises under the Western Teeth, runs along the edge of the Deepwood and east to the meeting of the waters.

features.name: The Brenn
features.notes: The river of the High Table. Leaves by the Table Gap.

features.name: The Sarn
features.notes: The great river. East through the Gap Vale, in many threads through the Rattlereed, then south-west, broad and slow, to the bay.

features.name: The Chalkwater
features.notes: Comes out of the limestone already a river.

features.name: The Aver
features.notes: Leaves the Sarn below the crossing and runs to the sea by itself.

features.name: The Pallow
features.notes: The steppe river, low in summer, braided at the ford.

features.name: The Sow Fen
features.notes: Reed and standing water between the wood and the river country. Eels.

features.name: Hartwall
features.notes: The walled town of the Thessen, where the wood meets the wet ground. About 3,400 within and close about the wall.

features.name: Stillgate
features.notes: The walled seat of the Ussel, built on older dressed stone. About 1,800.

features.name: Underfold
features.notes: A hamlet in the next fold east. About 600.

features.name: Lowstair
features.notes: A hamlet in the fold to the south-west. About 500.

features.name: Brennhal
features.notes: The town of the Arroway on the basin floor by the river. About 3,000.

features.name: Larchstead
features.notes: Terraced hamlet on the eastern slope.

features.name: Oatsteps
features.notes: Terraced hamlet on the western slope.

features.name: The Table Gap
features.notes: The narrow way where the Brenn leaves the basin.

features.name: Bell Pass
features.notes: High, closed by snow half the year. An iron is struck here.

features.name: Kite Pass
features.notes: The eastern way into the basin.

features.name: Smoke Pass
features.notes: The western way into the basin.

features.name: Thaw Saddle
features.notes: A wide saddle with a trodden way over it and many cairns.

features.name: The Cairn Way
features.notes: A trodden way from the saddle down to the lee side, marked with cairns.

features.name: Greybay Hold
features.notes: A winter hold of the Column: walled rock shelters and cellars cut in rock.

features.name: Kettle Hold
features.notes: A winter hold of the Column.

features.name: Lee Hold
features.notes: A winter hold of the Column.

features.name: Farcellar
features.notes: A winter hold of the Column, the easternmost.

features.name: Lampford
features.known_to: the Lowlamp; road traders; the Sallow
features.notes: The winter ground of the Lowlamp at the ford of the Pallow, which they call the Ford. About 5,000 in winter, a few hundred in the open seasons.

features.name: The Pale Road
features.notes: A road on hard pale ground, older than any town on it.

features.name: The Trough Station
features.notes: A length of old wall with no roof and a stone trough by the road. A way-station whose builders are not remembered.

features.name: Stakewater
features.notes: The town of the Weirfolk on the high bank at the one good crossing of the Sarn, which they call the Crossing. About 5,000 with its near fields.

features.name: The Toll Stone
features.notes: A worn standing stone at the crossing, older than any bridge footing there. Not a ruin: a stone.

features.name: Tallyford
features.notes: The town of the Marrans at the lowest ford of the Sarn. About 1,700 through the hard months, more at the autumn fair.

features.name: Keelstrand
features.notes: Boat shore on the bay.

features.name: The Meadow Road
features.notes: An old rutted road along the Sarn from the ford to the crossing.

features.name: The Strand Road
features.notes: A road west toward the limestone, sunk in places under newer ground.

features.name: The Old Weighhouse
features.notes: Footings of a great hall of a league of ford towns.

features.name: unnamed town
features.known_to: the unnamed people; a few charcoal buyers
features.notes: The town of the player's people. Unnamed until play names it. About 3,000 in the town, the rest in farms and clearings round it. A burial ground and orchard at its edge, unnamed.

features.name: The Coppice Track
features.notes: A worn track, wide enough for two abreast, from the town out through coppice toward the low country.

features.name: Swallet Mouth
features.notes: A great sinkhole with a cave in its side. Below: galleries in the limestone that run for miles south and west (the underground, data only).

features.name: The Long Bones
features.known_to: the unnamed people, as a place to avoid
features.notes: Something enormous and dead in the rock, too large to be sure it is bones. Not a ruin.

features.name: Averley
features.notes: The old walled city of the kingdom of Averley. About 9,000.

features.name: Saltsteps
features.notes: Salt pans cut in the rock of the headland. About 1,200.

features.name: Nettlebridge
features.notes: A bridge village on the Aver.

features.name: The Warm Stone
features.notes: Not a ruin: a stone, blue-grey, warm, heavy for its size, that fell in open hill pasture the night the gods came down.

features.name: Hethmoot
features.notes: The winter meeting ground of the Hethren. Tents and a few stone pens.

features.name: The Sleeper
features.notes: Not a mountain: a sleeping beast, visibly a beast, a mile or two long, lying in the hollow of the Dun Back. The hill mass round it has taken its outline.

features.name: Nightstake
features.notes: The largest of the reed folk's stilt places.

features.name: Graithdeep
features.known_to: the Graith; the Column, as a place not to enter
features.notes: The mouth of the Graith's deep halls. Below: chambers and long ways under the eastern range (the underground, data only).

features.name: The Shut Pass
features.notes: A pass closed by an old fall no one living saw.

features.name: Three-Age Fort
features.notes: A pass-fort of three ages, each built on the last.

features.name: The Sealed Door
features.notes: A door in rock, shut. Not a cave: a door.

features.name: Door Under Root
features.notes: A door in rock under a fallen tree, shut from the inside. Not a cave: a door.

features.name: Hollow Seat
features.notes: A walled seat of an older people, emptied without a siege.

features.name: The Old Stair
features.notes: A stair cut in rock going up into trees, above Stillgate.

features.name: The Walked-Round Shrine
features.notes: An untended shrine in the wood. The Thessen walk round it.

features.name: The King's Stair
features.notes: Terraces and a broken hall of the old basin kingdom.

features.name: The Sunk Road
features.notes: An old road that goes nowhere now, north from Averley toward the Table Gap, lost under turf across the heath. Parts of it run underground (data only).

features.name: Deepway Mouth
features.notes: An old road that goes into the range and under it (the underground, data only).
